Hi Ethan / Pinecrest security team,

Thanks for the request — attaching a single consolidated packet to address the items in your annex checklist: a current subprocessor manifest, an updated dataflow diagram that highlights cross-border hops, and a short KMS custody attestation.

High-level notes:
- Subprocessors: we list both hosted providers and vendor-managed services; each row includes the processing category and whether they have access to persistent PII.
- KMS: keys for customer data are in customer-specific key rings in the US (primary) with failover key material in a separate HSM-managed region per our key-rotation policy. The attached attestation summarizes custody and rotation dates.
- Dataflow: the diagram highlights where prefix caching occurs and where ephemeral logs are stored (all logs are redacted and retained per our retention matrix).

Next steps for us: Priya to provide the redline of the standard DPA annex where we map each Pinecrest ask to the evidence item (attached). Marcus and Jordan are copied for technical clarifications.

Attachments: [subprocessor_manifest_v2.csv (text/csv)], [dataflow_diagram_v3.png (image/png)], [kms-attestation-stub.pdf (application/pdf)]

If helpful, we can jump on a 30 min call today to walk through the diagram and point to specific controls.

Thanks,

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick packet. A few clarifying Qs after an initial pass: 

1) For the subprocessor manifest, can you add a column that indicates whether each subprocessors' environment is within the EU/EEA, US, or APAC (we flagged a couple that look like they may replicate logs outside the EEA)?
2) For KMS custody: we need a short note confirming whether any customer key material is escrowed with a third party or only stored within Redwood-managed HSMs.
3) Dataflow: can you call out exactly where debug logs containing sampled PII may be persisted (we need retention periods by environment).

Would also appreciate a clean redline of the DPA Annex (not a tracked version) we can circulate internally; we prefer a single Word doc.

We can do a call at 4pm PT today if that works for your team.

Best,

Ethan — quick technical follow-up inline: 

1) Subprocessor locations: good catch. The manifest has a geography column but Ill expand it to three explicit fields (primary region, replication region, logs storage region). The two vendors you flagged (edge-cache provider and monitoring vendor) replicate telemetry to a US analytics cluster; we can mark replication and provide contractual restrictions we maintain on the replicas.

2) KMS custody: customer key material is generated and stored in Redwoods HSM-managed key rings (no third-party escrow). We do have a key archival export procedure used for disaster recovery that requires multi-party approval and is logged; that process is governed by our SOC2 controls. Ill include the procedure name and an exported artifacts list in the KMS-stub.

3) Debug logs: sampled debug traces are written to an ephemeral debug store for 7 days by default, then truncated and redacted; a subset is forwarded to our analytics pipeline for 90 days. We can add a table to the dataflow diagram with per-environment retention columns.

Will push an updated manifest + diagram by 2:30pm PT.

-Marcus
